current_row.boundary_rationale: The row opens on the first of four repeated “in that day” formulas structuring the unit: "וְהָיָ֣ה בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא יִשְׁרֹ֤ק יְהוָה֙ לַזְּב֔וּב אֲשֶׁ֥ר בִּקְצֵ֖ה יְאֹרֵ֣י מִצְרָ֑יִם וְלַ֨דְּבוֹרָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֖ר בְּאֶ֥רֶץ אַשּֽׁוּר" (oshb:Isa.7.18, byte tier), matching “It will happen in that day that Yahweh will whistle for the fly that is in the uttermost part of the rivers of Egypt, and for the bee that is in the land of Assyria.” (web:Isa.7.18). Its extended opener, "וְהָיָ֣ה בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא" (oshb:Isa.7.18, byte tier), is accent-stripped-identical to the extended opener of web:Isa.7.21, "וְהָיָ֖ה בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֑וּא" (oshb:Isa.7.21, byte tier), and of web:Isa.7.23, though the three are not byte-identical to one another (sweep: 13 verses book-wide at the extended, accent-stripped form; 45 verses book-wide at the bare “in that day” form). web:Isa.7.20 opens on the shorter "בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֡וּא" (oshb:Isa.7.20, byte tier) without the leading element and is a different attested form, disclosed rather than counted with the other three. The seam is best argued not from the day-formula's own recurrence, which recurs across web:Isa.7.18-Isa.7.25 and which cannot discriminate the cut on its own, but from a frame-mode shift at MT 7:18 itself: the narrated direct-address scene that has framed the intervening speech since web:Isa.7.1 gives way here to an impersonal formulaic oracle cycle that names no speaker and addresses no one directly. These four images bind the fly/bee, razor, and briers-and-thorns pictures into one oracle cycle addressed to the same audience as the preceding narrative but marked off from it by their own repeated formula rather than a fresh scene. The cycle runs to “All the hills that were cultivated with the hoe, you shall not come there for fear of briers and thorns; but it shall be for the sending out of oxen, and for sheep to tread on.” (web:Isa.7.25), where chapter 8’s sign-act command (web:Isa.8.1) opens a new divine-command frame.
current_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: An alternative atomizes the row into four separate rows, one per 'in that day' onset (web:Isa.7.18, web:Isa.7.20, web:Isa.7.21, web:Isa.7.23), but the four share one addressee and one cumulative judgment image, lacking any addressee shift or divine-frame renewal between them, arguing one coherent oracle unit under the over-split-risk rule.
current_row.literature_type_guess: four-part 'in that day' addendum: fly, bee, razor, and briers
current_row.wj_or_red_letter_considered: not applicable in the OT substrate
current_row.device_notes: A tier-3 parashah witness marks a petuchah at oshb:Isa.7.17; a setumah at oshb:Isa.7.20; and a petuchah at oshb:Isa.7.25; this is single-witness corroboration, disclosed for symmetry, and it did not drive this boundary.

items.claim: The row's nominated front-seam warrant - an "impersonal formulaic oracle cycle that names no speaker and addresses no one directly" - is contradicted twice inside the row's own boundary_rationale and by the bytes of the row's own closing verse.
items.proposed_change: PROPOSAL ONLY: delete the "addresses no one directly" clause; re-argue the front seam from the verse-initial oracle-frame onset "{718_ext}" (oshb:Isa.7.18, byte tier) taken together with the close of the named-participant narrative scene at MT 7:17, and reconsider confidence (currently medium with frontier_flag_considered false) once the warrant is restated. No span change proposed.
items.adjudicator_grounds: All the contradictions re-derive inside this one row's fields. The load-bearing front-seam warrant ('best argued not from the day-formula's own recurrence ... but from a frame-mode shift', characterising the cycle as one that 'names no speaker and addresses no one directly') is followed two sentences later by 'one oracle cycle addressed to the same audience as the preceding narrative'; the rejected alternative adds 'the four share one addressee ... lacking any addressee shift'; and the row's own closing quotation renders the direct address the warrant denies — “you shall not come there for fear of briers and thorns;” (web:Isa.7.25) — against "לֹֽא תָב֣וֹא שָׁ֔מָּה" at oshb:Isa.7.25 (byte tier, collate-verified). With no morphology layer staged, the 2ms/3fs parse of the form cannot be machine-settled from the pointed bytes, which itself disqualifies the characterisation as a seam-carrier; the in-field self-contradiction stands under either parse. High confirmed: the row's nominated front-seam warrant is byte-false under its own quoted witness and self-contradicted in-field. The seam placement is not the defect — "וְהָיָ֣ה בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא" opens oshb:Isa.7.18 verse-initial (byte tier), and its accent_stripped identity with the openers of oshb:Isa.7.21 and oshb:Isa.7.23 collate-verifies at that tier — so the cure is the proposed re-argument plus the confidence reconsideration, not a respan.

readjudication.grounds: One source occurrence with P02-010#1 (the shared 7:17|7:18 seam); ruled coherently with it — same both-sides derivation, same outcome. The proposal's 718_ext placeholder resolves to וְהָיָ֣ה בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא (oshb:Isa.7.18, tokens 1-3, byte tier; the slice's resolution string is byte-equal to the source splice) and the item is ruled with that text. LEFT (the preceding unit's close): יָבִ֨יא יְהוָ֜ה עָלֶ֗יךָ וְעַֽל עַמְּךָ֮ וְעַל בֵּ֣ית אָבִיךָ֒ (oshb:Isa.7.17, byte tier) — three 2ms pronominal suffixes closing the named-participant scene (suffix scan: exactly three), PE at Isa.7.17 in the staged parashah inventory (single witness, tier-3). RIGHT (this row's own opening verse): וְהָיָ֣ה בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא verse-initial (byte tier; 5 verses byte, 13 accent_stripped including oshb:Isa.7.21 and oshb:Isa.7.23 — the row's own tier-labelled recurrence digits re-verify — and the bare skeleton 45 verses), followed by the third-person announcement יִשְׁרֹ֤ק יְהוָה֙ (byte tier), with 0 second-person suffixes across oshb:Isa.7.18-7.25: formula onset plus person shift at the seam verse itself. The front seam is warranted from both sides by bytes the row already splices; the placement is not the defect. The defect re-derives inside this row's own boundary_rationale, but at a lower weight than filed. The field first demotes the formula ('cannot discriminate the cut on its own'), then rests the seam on the frame-mode characterisation, then two sentences later says the cycle is 'marked off from it by their own repeated formula rather than a fresh scene' — re-asserting the formula it demoted — and calls the cycle 'addressed to the same audience as the preceding narrative' while the rejected alternative adds 'the four share one addressee ... lacking any addressee shift'; read with 'addressee' as the oracle's target these are loose rather than flatly contradictory, but the field is muddled at its load-bearing point. The byte test of 'addresses no one directly' is open, not false: תָב֣וֹא in לֹֽא תָב֣וֹא שָׁ֔מָּה יִרְאַ֖ת שָׁמִ֣יר וָשָׁ֑יִת (oshb:Isa.7.25, byte tier) is 2ms/3fs-ambiguous in the pointed bytes with no morphology layer staged; the 3fs parse with the following feminine construct noun as subject is byte-available and parallels יָ֣בוֹא שָׁ֑מָּה (oshb:Isa.7.24, byte tier); the row's own closing quotation renders it second person — “you shall not come there for fear of briers and thorns;” (web:Isa.7.25) — while the same witness renders תִּסְפֶּֽה (oshb:Isa.7.20) and תִּֽהְיֶ֥ה (oshb:Isa.7.24), the cycle's other two taw-prefixed forms, as third person; the row neither argues the parse nor reconciles its own quoted witness, so under the tier-disclosure standard the clause is unsupported and witness-contradicted as written. 'Names no speaker' holds (no koh-amar, neum, or amar/vayomer-plus-YHWH site in oshb:Isa.7.18-7.25 in the divine-speech census; the next narrative onset is וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֵלַ֔י at oshb:Isa.8.1, byte tier). The prior adjudication applied the byte-false-load-bearing-warrant rule to the 7:25 rendering and the in-field wording; the complete test finds the seam-kernel of the row's warrant (the shift at MT 7:18 itself) byte-true and the seam twice warranted in-row, leaving an unsupported over-generalisation and muddled ordering in the load-bearing field — the defective-warrant-over-uncontested-seam class this queue rates medium. Downgrade to medium, coherently with P02-010#1. Cure as proposed, no span change: delete the 'addresses no one directly' clause, re-argue the front seam from the 7:18 formula onset taken with the 7:17 second-person close (PE as tier-3 corroboration), settle the field's own stance on the formula, and reconsider confidence (medium, frontier_flag_considered false) once restated.

items.claim: The "45 verses book-wide at the bare “in that day” form" digit carries no tier label and is wrong under the only tier named in its own parenthetical.
items.proposed_change: PROPOSAL ONLY: label the digit's tier - "45 verses book-wide at the bare form, consonantal-skeleton tier" - or restate as "41 verses ... accent-stripped". No span change.
items.adjudicator_grounds: Re-swept from splices of oshb:Isa.7.18. The extended opener "וְהָיָ֣ה בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא" (byte tier at its own verse) sweeps 13 verses at accent_stripped tier (sweep: verse counts) — the row's first digit re-verifies exactly. The bare form "בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא" (byte tier at its own verse) sweeps 12 verses byte / 41 accent_stripped / 45 skeleton (sweep: verse counts); the four verses separating 45 from 41 are exactly MT 2:11, 2:17, 3:7, 29:18, where the form's meteg-bearing pointing survives accent stripping — the staged accent_stripped tier retains meteg, stripping cantillation only — and blocks the accent-tier match, precisely as the finding states. So the shipped 45-verse bare-form digit is the consonantal-skeleton count standing with no tier label of its own inside a parenthetical whose only named tier is accent-stripped, under which the true digit is 41 — a violation of the tier-label law that binds every recurrence claim. Medium is right: the row expressly declines to argue the seam from this recurrence in the same field, so the digit is not load-bearing; either proposed restatement cures it.

current_row.boundary_rationale: The unit opens where the scene turns from darkened lands into light, at כִּ֣י לֹ֣א מוּעָף֮ לַאֲשֶׁ֣ר מוּצָ֣ק לָהּ֒ (oshb:Isa.8.23, byte tier), rendered “But there shall be no more gloom for her who was in anguish. In the former time, he brought into contempt the land of Zebulun and the land of Naphtali; but in the latter time he has made it glorious, by the way of the sea, beyond the Jordan, Galilee of the nations.” (web:Isa.9.1) = oshb:Isa.8.23; the causal particle opening that verse recurs verse-initially inside the span at oshb:Isa.9.3 (= web:Isa.9.4), oshb:Isa.9.4 (= web:Isa.9.5) and oshb:Isa.9.5 (= web:Isa.9.6), so the seam rests on the turn from darkened lands to light and glory the verse carries, not on the particle. A fresh nominal subject then opens the following verse, הָעָם֙ הַהֹלְכִ֣ים בַּחֹ֔שֶׁךְ (oshb:Isa.9.1, byte tier) = web:Isa.9.2, and the address turns second person at הִרְבִּ֣יתָ הַגּ֔וֹי (oshb:Isa.9.2, byte tier) = web:Isa.9.3, continued by הַחִתֹּ֖תָ (oshb:Isa.9.3, byte tier) = web:Isa.9.4; the unit is read as one sustained declaration, not because no fresh subject or addressee arises — both do — but because the chain of causal ki-clauses that follows (כִּ֣י אֶת עֹ֣ל סֻבֳּל֗וֹ, oshb:Isa.9.3 = web:Isa.9.4; כִּ֤י כָל סְאוֹן֙, oshb:Isa.9.4 = web:Isa.9.5) restates the same reason as the opening light and the multiplied joy, before the birth clause returns to third person, כִּי יֶ֣לֶד יֻלַּד (oshb:Isa.9.5, byte tier) = web:Isa.9.6, without a further break in the argument. The throne-naming clause reads פֶּ֠לֶא יוֹעֵץ֙ אֵ֣ל גִּבּ֔וֹר אֲבִי עַ֖ד שַׂר שָׁלֽוֹם (oshb:Isa.9.5, byte tier), rendered “His name will be called Wonderful Counselor, Mighty God, Everlasting Father, Prince of Peace.” (web:Isa.9.6 = oshb:Isa.9.5); an OSHB exegesis note sits at this same verse (oshb:Isa.9.5), single-witness apparatus only, never text bytes, and is disclosed rather than argued as content. The unit closes at the government-increase clause, which the letter bytes stage as a doubled ketiv/qere token pair לםרבה לְמַרְבֵּ֨ה (oshb:Isa.9.6, byte tier) — the ketiv form carries a final mem in medial position; the quote engages both staged forms, not one alone — rendered “The zeal of Yahweh of Armies will perform this.” (web:Isa.9.7 = oshb:Isa.9.6). No addressee or subject marker reopens before web:Isa.9.8's fresh declarative sentence, so the throne clause stays inside this unit.
current_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the light-dawning announcement from the throne-naming and its government clause is rejected because the chain of coordinated ki-clauses keeps both halves inside one argument for the nation's joy.
current_row.wj_or_red_letter_considered: not applicable in the OT substrate
current_row.device_notes: A Masoretic setumah break follows oshb:Isa.9.6 (= web:Isa.9.7), tier-3 single-witness corroboration only, for a close already argued from the ki-chain and the fresh subject at web:Isa.9.8; it is never treated as the driver. A ketiv/qere note also sits at oshb:Isa.9.2 (= web:Isa.9.3), inside this unit's own span; it was checked before slicing near that verse and is disclosed here without a content claim resting on either reading. The medial final-mem in the doubled token is letter bytes plus ketiv/qere apparatus, not a special-letter seg of any size. The referent of the throne names (a court style exalting a Davidic king, versus a fuller messianic reading) is not settled by this boundary decision and is held open.

items.claim: The front seam at MT 8:22|MT 8:23 (= web:Isa.8.22|web:Isa.9.1) rests on a thematic tonal turn after the row itself disqualifies the only formal marker standing at MT 8:23.
items.proposed_change: PROPOSAL ONLY: re-argue the front seam from the temporal-contrast frame in oshb:Isa.8.23's (= web:Isa.9.1's) own bytes, or drop confidence from medium to medium_low given that the span carries MT 9:5-6 (= web:Isa.9.6-9.7), a registered expected-low-confidence region. No span change proposed.
items.adjudicator_grounds: Re-derived both ways from bytes. כִּ֣י opens oshb:Isa.8.23 (= web:Isa.9.1) verse-initially (byte tier), and the particle's skeleton also opens oshb:Isa.9.3 (= web:Isa.9.4), oshb:Isa.9.4 (= web:Isa.9.5) and oshb:Isa.9.5 (= web:Isa.9.6) as each verse's first token (token-bound skeleton tier, 3/3) — the row's own showing disqualifies the only formal marker it names. What remains as shipped is thematic ('the seam rests on the turn from darkened lands to light and glory the verse carries, not on the particle' — verified verbatim); no ruled tier-1 class (frame onset, speech formula, vocative, imperative onset, addressee shift) is named at the seam verse, and the row's oss key oracle_frame.light_dawning_onset names no ruled frame class of the book's tier-1 spine (massa/hoy/koh-amar/neum/vocative/imperative/addressee-shift), so it supplies no formal onset either; pmarks_Isa.json re-checked: no parashah entry at MT 8:22 (tier-3 layer, single-witness, absence never counterevidence). The unused byte-anchored candidate is real: כָּעֵ֣ת הָרִאשׁ֗וֹן and וְהָאַחֲר֖וֹן הִכְבִּ֑יד both collate at byte tier inside oshb:Isa.8.23 (= web:Isa.9.1), in that order (byte offsets 43 and 112), and neither run appears anywhere in the shipped rationale. The seam's placement itself is uncontested (the preceding row closes at web:Isa.8.22; no span change filed), and the span carries the registered expected-low-confidence stack at oshb:Isa.9.5-9.6 (= web:Isa.9.6-9.7): defective front-seam warrant, not alone load-bearing — confirm at medium.

readjudication.grounds: Both sides re-derived; every ref here is in zone A and dual-cited. RIGHT (the row's own opening verse): כִּ֣י לֹ֣א מוּעָף֮ לַאֲשֶׁ֣ר מוּצָ֣ק לָהּ֒ opens oshb:Isa.8.23 (= web:Isa.9.1) (byte tier); the particle also opens oshb:Isa.9.3 (= web:Isa.9.4), oshb:Isa.9.4 (= web:Isa.9.5) and oshb:Isa.9.5 (= web:Isa.9.6) inside the span, as the row itself shows, so the row disqualifies its only formal marker and rests the seam on 'the turn from darkened lands to light and glory the verse carries, not on the particle' — verified verbatim. No ruled onset class (hoy, hinneh, koh-amar, neum, massa header, imperative, vocative, addressee shift, verse-initial temporal formula) stands in that verse; the temporal-contrast pair כָּעֵ֣ת הָרִאשׁ֗וֹן ... וְהָאַחֲר֖וֹן הִכְבִּ֑יד (oshb:Isa.8.23 = web:Isa.9.1, byte tier) is mid-verse content the row leaves unused, and it is not a ruled onset class either. LEFT (the preceding unit's close, which the onset-only finding never weighed): וְהִנֵּ֨ה צָרָ֤ה וַחֲשֵׁכָה֙ מְע֣וּף צוּקָ֔ה וַאֲפֵלָ֖ה מְנֻדָּֽח (oshb:Isa.8.22, byte tier) is a descriptive close — no refrain, no signature, no imperative, no formula — and the staged parashah inventory records no seg at Isa.8.22 or Isa.8.23 (nearest: SAMEKH at Isa.8.18 and SAMEKH at Isa.9.6 = web:Isa.9.7; single witness, absence weighed as nothing); the preceding row's own rear-seam warrant is the same tonal reversal read from the other side. So the complete test finds NO ruled tier-1 signal on either side of MT 8:22|8:23 (= web:Isa.8.22|web:Isa.9.1): the finding is confirmed, not rescued. The seam's only byte-anchored relation binds the two verses as much as it turns them — the root-level antithesis of מְע֣וּף צוּקָ֔ה (oshb:Isa.8.22, byte tier) against מוּעָף֮ and מוּצָ֣ק (oshb:Isa.8.23 = web:Isa.9.1, byte tier): form-distinct at skeleton tier (sweeps: the 8:22 gloom and anguish spellings stand at 1 and 2 verses, the 8:23 pair at 1 and 1; no two of the four share a skeleton), a lemma-level echo disclosed by neither row and not a ruled device. The nearest onset of the class the neighbouring rows accept as a driver — a fresh grammatical subject (web:Isa.9.8 = oshb:Isa.9.7; web:Isa.11.1) — stands one verse INSIDE the row, הָעָם֙ הַהֹלְכִ֣ים בַּחֹ֔שֶׁךְ at oshb:Isa.9.1 (= web:Isa.9.2) (byte tier), which the row discloses and absorbs into its ki-chain argument; the second-person turn הִרְבִּ֣יתָ at oshb:Isa.9.2 (= web:Isa.9.3) (byte tier; a K/Q verse, checked before slicing) is two verses in. The cut as placed coincides with the WEB chapter seam, while the MT chapter seam falls one verse later at that fresh-subject onset — tier-4 in both traditions, evidence for nothing, recorded only so that no repair leans on it. Severity: the prior adjudication ('defective front-seam warrant, not alone load-bearing') was already two-sided in substance — it checked the left for marks; the complete test adds that the left carries no ruled close and that the one cross-seam link is lemma-level continuity. Medium is confirmed rather than raised because the finding contests the warrant, not the placement (no respan filed; both adjacent rows cut here on the same ground), the row holds frontier_flag_considered true at medium and discloses the internal fresh-subject rival, and the remedy is proportionate — but only the confidence branch of the proposal survives the test that killed the original: re-arguing from the temporal-contrast pair would swap one non-ruled content signal for another, mid-verse and bound to the preceding verse by the gloom/anguish antithesis; medium_low is the honest band for a span whose front seam has no ruled warrant on either side and which carries the registered hazard stack at oshb:Isa.9.5-9.6 (= web:Isa.9.6-9.7): exegesis note at MT 9:5, K/Q plus SAMEKH at MT 9:6, K/Q at MT 9:2 (= web:Isa.9.3).

The doubled pair לםרבה לְמַרְבֵּ֨ה collates at byte tier and opens oshb:Isa.9.6 (= web:Isa.9.7) at byte offset 0; WEB's rendering of that clause opens the verse — “Of the increase of his government” (web:Isa.9.7 = oshb:Isa.9.6), normalized position 0 — while the row's paired gloss “The zeal of Yahweh of Armies will perform this.” (web:Isa.9.7 = oshb:Isa.9.6) is the verse-final sentence (normalized position 212 of 259) rendering קִנְאַ֛ת יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת תַּעֲשֶׂה זֹּֽאת (oshb:Isa.9.6 = web:Isa.9.7, byte tier, verse-final): splice and gloss render disjoint clauses, so the shipped 'rendered' is false under any parse — the core defect, exactly as filed.
